title: Synthesize minimal CCP policy proposal
description: Produce source-linked Probably Right Thing recommendation separating link-quality SF selection, receiver rendezvous, density-aware control traffic and airtime congestion admission. Keep proposed wire/scheduling changes distinct from settled decisions; avoid invented numeric thresholds, perfect scheduling claims and new negotiation frameworks.
acceptance_criteria: Proposal covers ordinary single-radio mesh and stronger gateway capabilities, fallback/desync, bounded queues and priorities, regulatory accounting, metrics uncertainty, and cheapest initial corrective revision; no spec edits or adjudication claim.
notes:
PROPOSAL ONLY, NOT ADJUDICATED: user requested static reasoning, not spec or implementation changes. Existing density-high and other decisions remain normative until explicitly superseded. Recommended direction: keep rendezvous stable; choose SF for link budget; respond to excess demand by admitting less airtime, not by channel concentration or longer packets.

1. Separate inputs: observed peer density guides conservative startup and control-traffic rate/scope; actual service/queue age/CCA contention guide airtime admission; receiver-side, directional link margin guides SF. Do not synthesize extra neighbors from weak RSSI or loss. Unknown/stale measurements remain unknown, not evidence of an idle or weak link. TX completion is not delivery; no blanket packet-loss estimate from absent baseline link ACKs.

2. Receiver owns the data rendezvous. Fresh authenticated rx_channel and the common channel plan/generation determine where to send. Deterministic fallback may depend on peer identity and shared plan/epoch, not sender-local density. Adjacent nodes can see9 and11 peers and otherwise choose incompatible data/CH0 paths. Keep home channels stable within a schedule generation; do not retune as a per-packet reaction to CCA failure. CH0 fallback is for discovery, unsupported/stale rendezvous, absent data channels or desync, not high headcount.

3. Use periodic common CH0 control/discovery windows and data windows rather than physically impossible continuous CH0 plus off-channel receive. One-radio nodes reserve actual receiver availability and cannot schedule overlapping TX/RX. A scheduled send is a rendezvous with next-hop receive opportunity, not merely sender TX permission. Reuse existing beacon/announce/slot assignment machinery, not a new per-packet reservation protocol. An advertised RX commitment wins over newly queued TX. Complete frame plus setup/turnaround/ACK when applicable and guard must fit; max-frame2346ms only covers canonical SF10 data plus50ms guard, not arbitrary extras. Control windows of overlapping DODAGs need compatible rendezvous or explicit extended-CH0 discovery; routing partitions alone do not isolate RF. Broadcast/multicast initially uses bounded common control opportunities. Loss of sync suppresses scheduled TX and returns to extended CH0 listening.

4. Hashes are candidates, not collision-free grants. With default8 slots, common SFN addition never separates equal hash residues. Actual assignments must resolve sender/receiver and parent-child conflicts; uncertain or unassigned access remains contended with bounded backoff, not claimed collision-free. Multiple channels buy concurrency only for independent feasible RX/TX pairs. Single-radio receiver serializes all arrivals regardless of channel count; multichannel gateway RX does not imply simultaneous multi-TX or limitless demodulation. Do not substitute network-wide lockstep hopping for parallel-channel capacity: it offers frequency diversity, not simultaneous links.

5. Regulatory and congestion limits are separate. Account every frame, forwarding copy, control packet and retry against the applicable regulatory channel-group budget. Different channels in one regulated group do not each earn a fresh allowance. Reserve bounded control airtime within legal limits; priority cannot bypass legality or create airtime. Bound queues, expire stale datagrams, coalesce explicitly replaceable position/status updates, reject/back-pressure when full, and pace lower-priority sources to actual service. Preserve settled best-effort custody and its own TTL/storage rules; do not turn telemetry into custody or invent delivery guarantees. Retain current conservative admissible ceilings for an initial revision rather than invent an untested congestion controller. More audible idle nodes is not necessarily more airtime load; busy few can saturate a receiver.

6. Lowest supported SF meeting directional link margin is the eventual adaptation goal, but it requires receiver confirmation and compatible PHY/slot timing. Do not use gateway queue load, density or unattributed packet loss to raise SF. Initial corrective profile should honor existing fixed SF10/profile01 and remove conflicting density-driven in-schedule ADR. Different SF is an explicit compatible profile/schedule transition with hysteresis and activation boundary, not unilateral retuning. An SF12-only route also needs a viable control/bootstrap profile, not just data SF12.

High-confidence static evidence is in5qtu.1:100B SF10/SF12 airtime1.026048/3.940352s; with36/18sec hourly budgets service35.09/4.57 frames/hour before control/retries. Airtime per success under an independent retry model is T/q; SF increase is worthwhile only for sufficient delivery improvement, not just load. Stability margin/coverage cannot be inferred from successful RX SNR alone.

Measurements/design detail still needed: feasible control cadence versus complete beacon cost and clock/guard uncertainty; collision repair/grant encoding and fairness at multiroot boundaries; SF margins and hysteresis; hidden-terminal/capture behavior; sampling windows for mobile/sleeping nodes; true gateway receive/transmit capacity and worst relay traffic cuts. Do not claim event-scale throughput, perfect scheduler fairness or zero loss from static reasoning. Rejected alternatives: threshold10->50 alone, local density controlling remote rendezvous, unconditional SF escalation for congestion, continuous all-channel/all-SF reception on one radio, adding buffers, and a wholesale new MAC framework. Source references: spec/02a-coordinated-capacity.md:76-111,369-488,533-633; spec/appendix-ccp12-hopping.md:62-87,226-259; spec/02a-tdma.md:13-42; spec/appendix-bufferbloat.md:45-105.
close_reason: Synthesized a minimal receiver-aware policy from two independent analyses and checked airtime calculations. Proposal, assumptions, rejected alternatives and measurement-dependent details retained explicitly as NOT ADJUDICATED. No source/spec/fixture changes or runtime-conformance claims.
